definitions.explanation: To insert or put something into a space or opening.

definitions.gloss: to bring refreshments or gifts (to someone working)
definitions.explanation: To bring food, drinks, or gifts to people who are working hard or to someone in detention. The noun form {差|さ}し{入|い}れ is commonly used.

examples.japanese: ⟦{鍵|かぎ}→鍵：02189_kagi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{鍵穴|かぎあな}→鍵穴：30443_kagiana⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{差|さ}し{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Insert the key into the keyhole.

examples.japanese: ⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{封筒|ふうとう}→封筒：02952_fuutou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{差|さ}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I slipped the letter into the envelope.

examples.japanese: ⟦コイン→コイン：10852_koin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{自動販売機|じどうはんばいき}→自動販売機：03078_jidouhanbaiki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{差|さ}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I inserted a coin into the vending machine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{残業|ざんぎょう}→残業：01071_zangyou⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{同僚|どうりょう}→同僚：01023_douryou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{差|さ}し{入|い}れ→差し入れ：08294_sashiire⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I brought refreshments to my colleagues working overtime.

examples.japanese: ⟦{留置場|りゅうちじょう}→留置場：30444_ryuuchijou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{本|ほん}→本：00111_hon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{差|さ}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I brought books to my friend in detention.

examples.japanese: ⟦{部活|ぶかつ}→部活：05377_bukatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{差|さ}し{入|い}れ→差し入れ：08294_sashiire⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦ジュース→ジュース：01033_juusu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}って→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: I brought juice as refreshments to the club practice.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: ⟦{他動詞|たどうし}→他動詞：10418_tadoushi⟧ (transitive). The thing inserted or brought takes ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ and the destination or recipient takes ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧.

COMPOUND VERB: Formed from ⟦{差|さ}す→差す：17637_sasu⟧ (to insert/extend) + ⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧ (to put in).

NOUN FORM: ⟦{差|さ}し{入|い}れ→差し入れ：08294_sashiire⟧ is commonly used as a noun meaning 'refreshments/gifts brought to someone' or 'the act of bringing such items.' In sense 2 the noun form is in fact far more common than the verb: people say ⟦{差|さ}し{入|い}れ→差し入れ：08294_sashiire⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ more often than {差|さ}し{入|い}れる.

SENSE 1 vs SENSE 2: Sense 1 (physical insertion) is neutral and slightly formal — everyday speech usually prefers plain ⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧ or ⟦{差|さ}す→差す：17637_sasu⟧. Sense 2 is the sense learners meet most often.

CULTURAL NOTE: Bringing ⟦{差|さ}し{入|い}れ→差し入れ：08294_sashiire⟧ to people working hard (such as during overtime, sports practice, or moving) is a common Japanese custom showing care and appreciation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・⟦{差|さ}し{入|い}れ→差し入れ：08294_sashiire⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}って→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧ (bring refreshments)
・⟦おやつ→おやつ：17921_oyatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{差|さ}し{入|い}れる (bring snacks)
・⟦{差|さ}し{入|い}れ→差し入れ：08294_sashiire⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧ (receive refreshments)
